title: Dart stuns Badosa to make second career semi-final
article_text:
Britain's Harriet Dart reached the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career when she fought back from a set down to beat fifth seed Paula Badosa at the Guangzhou Open in China.

The 30-year-old triumphed 3-6 6-2 6-4 against Spain's Badosa - ranked 54 places above her - in two hours and 15 minutes at Nansha International Tennis Centre.

Dart's first appearance in the semi-finals of a tour event was in the Transylvania Open in Cluj-Napoca, where she lost in straight sets to Karolina Pliskova.

She will face 16-year-old Chinese wildcard Sun Xinran in the last four on Saturday.

"It's been a very long time since I've been in the business end of the tournament so I am really excited for that," Dart said.

"Tennis is so stressful, so to have the opportunity to compete again on Saturday is a great opportunity for me."

Dart, who came through qualifying and beat second-seed Janice Tjen in the previous round, lost her opening service game in the first set but broke back and drew level at 3-3.

However, former world number two Badosa broke Dart's serve again to take a 5-3 lead and held her serve to close out the set.

The pair exchanged breaks at the start of the second set before Dart seized the upper hand to level at 1-1.

Badosa, who required two medical timeouts during the match as she appeared to struggle with the heat, saved a match point at 5-3 in the deciding set and then broke Dart's serve.

But the Spaniard, ranked 61st in the world, was running on empty in her next service game, as Dart won it to love.

"It was an incredible battle. I thought Paula started really strongly. I was always behind, and knew it was going to be an incredibly tough match," Dart added.

"I really needed to hang in there during the tough moments and wait for a chance. Luckily I was able to take my chance, and I am very excited to be in the semi-finals."

Dart reached a career high of 70th in the world in 2024, having made the Wimbledon third round and US Open second round, but has been languishing outside the top 100 for the vast majority of the past two seasons.

The run from Guangzhou qualifying to the last four puts her on the cusp of the top 100 once again, meaning she has a good chance of going straight into the main draw of the Australian Open in January without needing to qualify.

That would be rich reward for a superb second half to the season, where she has struck the ball consistently well and continued to grow in confidence.

Working with former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli has been a big factor in Dart's resurgence.

The pair live close to each other and began working together earlier this year. Dart has enjoyed soaking up the knowledge and experience imparted by the French former world number seven in their ad hoc coaching partnership.

Dart says she has also benefitted from Bartoli still "hitting a good ball" in practice.

The arrangement has helped Dart win 17 of her 22 tour-level matches on the hard courts since Wimbledon, taking her overall record on the WTA Tour this season to 21 victories from 32 matches - the highest winning percentage of her career.

Statement: Munster issue statement after Tadhg Furlong cleared of wrongdoing
article_text:
Munster Rugby have broken their silence after Tadhg Furlong escaped a ban following his disciplinary hearing, with the province issuing a pointed statement in support of Gavin Coombes.

The Ireland prop was cleared of foul play on Thursday night following an incident during Leinster's 24-18 victory over Munster.

Coombes alleged that Furlong had grabbed him in the groin area during the first half at the Aviva Stadium.

The incident was reviewed by the television match official before Furlong was subsequently cited under Law 9.27.

However, an independent disciplinary committee unanimously dismissed the complaint, finding that the 33-year-old had not committed an act of foul play.

Munster have now responded, making it clear their support for Coombes remains unchanged.

"Munster Rugby acknowledges the decision published on Thursday night by the Independent Disciplinary Committee."

"Gavin Coombes continues to have the full backing of the club."

Interim chief executive Avan Lee also appeared to take aim at public comments made during the disciplinary process.

"The priority this week was to back Gavin and for the club to stand behind him, and that position has not changed.

"We believe it is important that independent disciplinary proceedings are allowed to conclude without unhelpful commentary from people with a clear influence over public perception.

"Respect for that process, and consideration for everyone directly involved should be paramount."

The comments follow public support for Furlong from former Ireland captain Johnny Sexton, who said earlier this week that he did not believe the prop would commit such an offence.

Munster did not identify anyone in their statement.

Importantly, the disciplinary committee also found that Coombes had given an honest account of his recollection of the incident.

It confirmed the complaint had been properly brought before the panel, despite ultimately clearing Furlong.

The decision means Furlong is available for Ireland's upcoming Nations Championship campaign.

Andy Farrell's side begin their November fixtures against Argentina, with the Leinster tighthead now free to feature.

title: PREM chiefs hold Monaco talks with Eddie Hearn as he targets more stars
article_text:
English rugby bosses want Eddie Hearn to become more involved in the sport, calling the boxing promoter a "force for good".

England back-row Henry Pollock and Scotland fly-half Finn Russell both signed with Hearn's agency Matchroom earlier this year, with Pollock recently featuring on the cover of Men's Health and Tatler magazines as part of Hearn's efforts to grow his profile. Hearn has previously spoken of his desire to "turbo-charge" the profile of rugby and its players.

The renowned promoter has now been tipped to have a greater influence on the game.

Prem Rugby chief executive Simon Massie-Taylor recently met with Hearn, saying that he expects his involvement in rugby to grow in the near future.

“I met Eddie,” said Massie-Taylor. “We [the Prem] were out in Monaco for a few things, actually, but one of them was that our international broadcasters were all there as part of the Sportel Conference, and CVC were doing something else.

"So, we took the liberty to go and see him. First of all, he’s enjoyed his initial chapter within rugby.

"He sees a load of positives with the sport. The athletes; he thinks they’re incredibly marketable, and he sees that rugby is on a great trajectory, and he’s very pro the Prem.

“I think his ambition goes beyond just representing top athletes; although, I’d expect him to represent some more of the top stars in the Prem, and he’ll do a good job for them.

"So, you start to move into other options that you could consider; whether that’s around events, big games, or something specifically commercial around the players across the league.

"We’ve got our own Prem media house now, which is like a rocket ship in terms of the content it’s producing and the value for sponsors; whether there’s a partnership around that.

“I don’t think he’s here to buy a rugby club, but he could definitely help introduce people to it and partner with that. So, there are a few different options we’re talking through.

"But, he doesn’t want to be a disruptor. He wants to work with the league, but he definitely wants to agitate for more growth.

"I think he sees a lot of potential. So I think he’s a really positive person to have in the environment, and it’s encouraging that he sees such positive signs.

"I’d like to see [Matchroom] more involved. I think they’ll be a force for good.”

title: Malcolm Marx confirms departure as Springboks World Cup winner makes 'difficult decision'
article_text:
Springboks star Malcolm Marx has confirmed he will leave Japanese side Kubota Spears at the end of the season after making what he described as a "difficult decision".

The two-time Rugby World Cup winner will return to South Africa when his contract expires in June 2027.

Marx, 32, has decided against extending his stay in Japan, citing family reasons.

The hooker will complete the 2026/27 campaign before bringing his time with Kubota Spears to an end.

His decision comes just months before the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

In a statement published on Kubota Spears' official website, Marx explained why he had decided to leave.

"Unfortunately, due to family reasons, I have made the difficult decision not to extend my contract beyond the 2026/27 season and will be returning to South Africa."

The 32-year-old also thanked the club and its supporters for making his family feel welcome during their time in Japan.

Marx has become one of the most respected hookers in world rugby, helping South Africa win consecutive World Cups in 2019 and 2023.

He was also named World Rugby Men's 15s Player of the Year in 2025.

The 93-cap international has played a major role in the Springboks' continued success under Rassie Erasmus.

Attention will now turn to where Marx plays his rugby next season.

Both the Bulls and Sharks have previously been linked with the experienced front-rower.

The Bulls have also been pursuing a deal, with a move to Pretoria potentially reuniting Marx with former Lions coach Johan Ackermann.

Meanwhile, SA Rugby Magazine reported on Friday that it understands Marx has already signed for the Bulls.

However, the Pretoria-based club has yet to officially announce a deal.

A return to South African rugby would represent a major signing for whichever side eventually secures his services.

For now, Marx remains committed to finishing his time in Japan before returning home.

With the 2027 World Cup approaching, his next move will certainly be one to watch.

title: Four things we’ve learnt from the SVNS 3 schedule announcement
article_text:
The SVNS 3 tournament for the 2026-27 HSBC SVNS season was confirmed earlier this week, with a bumper weekend of fun in the sun set to occur in the final weekend of November.

Running alongside the HSBC SVNS Series opener, the chasing pack of regional sevens tournament winners will be playing for the chance to move up to SVNS 2 in January: with Olympic and SVNS World Championship qualification also in the mix.

RugbyPass breaks down the key talking points following the announcement, and which teams have the potential to qualify for the next level.

It’s crazy to think that the first iteration of the SVNS 3 tournament was only in January this year, yet the promise shown for this format to expose rising nations to higher levels of sevens rugby speaks volumes that fans will see a second weekend this year.

The confidence in SVNS 3 is for good reason, with the 2025-26 iteration seeing two sides make it all the way from SVNS 3 to the SVNS World Championship: South Africa Women and Argentina Women.

The success of those two sides would have likely impressed the powers that be at World Rugby, showing that the tiered format can lead to rapid improvement.

Those two sides will be likely starting their season in SVNS 2 this year – and with the 2026 season under their belts will be in a better position to push for SVNS Series qualification; but should a SVNS 3 side get on a similar run, it makes the upcoming SVNS 2 tournament more intriguing.

At the time of writing, 11 teams have been confirmed to take the field in Dubai, starting with Hong Kong China, Canada, Italy, Chile, Zimbabwe and Samoa in the men’s competition.

While several sides also appeared in last year’s tournament, the injection of Chile and Zimbabwe as new arrivals is set to turn a few heads, given the promise both sides have shown in their respective regional tournaments.

The women’s competition is awaiting one more side to confirm their place, with China, Mexico, Poland, Colombia and Samoa all vying for SVNS 2 qualification.

With China having made it to SVNS 2 last year before finishing in last place, the side will look to bounce back after a promising regional campaign, which saw them finish as runners up to Japan – but ask plenty of questions of the SVNS Series side.

With new teams in abundance in both tournaments, the opportunities come for more developing nations to press their case, and great stories in the form of rising rugby nations like the Germany men’s side making the SVNS World Championship format.

Hanging over the SNVS 3 format this season as well as the chance for higher honours in the HSBC SVNS format is the chance to qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The sides in SVNS 3 will be viewing their time in this tournament as critical, with the opportunity to play against higher level opposition a chance that cannot afford to be missed.

With the Olympics one of the highest mountains players can ascend to in the sevens format, even making qualification for LA would be massive for any developing sevens program, even if a side doesn’t end up on the podium.

The promise of Olympic qualification will likely add extra colour to both SVNS 3 and SVNS 2 over the next few months, as sides look to put their best form out on the paddock.

Lastly, with Dubai Sevens being one of the biggest events on the sevens calendar, the decision to also run SVNS 3 concurrently only adds to the occasion in the desert.

Fans will have the chance to not only see the current best sides in the world at The Sevens Stadium, but also get a first hand look at the sides looking to make it to the highest level.

The experience will also be a valuable one for the SVNS 3 sides, giving them a perfect opportunity to size up the best in the world and see the small things they do that make them such dangerous outfits.

It will make the final weekend of November a true festival of rugby in the desert – one that fans will flock to from all over the world, and a bucket list event for any international sevens player.

title: Creditor demands R110.7 million from South African rugby union — Daily Maverick
article_text:
Creditor demands R110.7 million from South African rugby union — Daily Maverick

In South Africa, Dream World Investments 401 has issued the Western Province Rugby Football Union (WPRFU) with a formal demand to pay R110,732,462.66 plus interest by November 12. If the debt is not settled or adequately secured, the company intends to file an application to liquidate the union, Daily Maverick reports.

Dream World’s lawyers sent the demand on October 22, 2026, in accordance with provisions of the Companies Act of 1973. The lender says that non-payment would create a legal presumption that the union is unable to pay its debts.

In August 2020, Dream World transferred R52,970,961 to Investec and R57,761,501.66 to Remgro, for a total of R110.73 million. The funds were intended to settle WPRFU’s debts and launch an agreement with developer Flyt for the development of the Newlands stadium site and adjacent properties.

As security for the obligations, the union’s trusts registered two mortgage bonds in favour of Dream World, each worth R250 million. One covers Newlands stadium and eight other properties in the Newlands area, while the other covers Mill House, Brookside and the union’s property in Oranjezicht.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

The agreement between the parties collapsed at the end of 2020. Since 2021, they have been engaged in litigation in the Western Cape High Court. The new demand does not replace those proceedings: Dream World retains claims for interest, fees and damages within the main case.

Dream World argues that the funds must be repaid regardless of the outcome of the dispute over the contracts. In its view, if the loan agreement was properly cancelled in December 2020, the amount is repayable; if the agreement never took effect or is invalid, the union received a benefit from the settlement of its debts. The company also states that if the agreement remains valid, the full amount became due in August 2024 — 48 months after the loan was granted.

WPRFU contests the claim. The union believes that the replacement of Flyt with Dream World as creditor was material, and that the loan agreement and the preliminary development agreement were interconnected parts of a single arrangement. In its court filing, it also argues that the documents contained uncertain provisions and that the terms of the transaction were contrary to public policy. WPRFU representatives declined to comment on the case to the media.

Dream World lawyer Menko Huksheima said that if the demand is not met by November 12, a formal liquidation application will be filed and served. According to him, in that event the union’s assets and commercial affairs would be managed by a liquidator or trustee.

title: Novak Djokovic's ATP Finals blow with Jan-Lennard Struff defeat
article_text:
Novak Djokovic's hopes of making a record 19th appearance at the ATP Finals have been dented by a surprise defeat against Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel.

Playing in the tournament for the first time in 15 years, the 39-year-old lost 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-5) - the first time he has been beaten by Struff in nine meetings.

"I knew I needed to go for it. There was only one way to play it. So, I was very, very happy," said the world number 27.

"I knew I had to play my best tennis to have a chance. The last eight times he beat me very, very easily. So, I'm very, very happy and pleased with the performance."

The year's top-eight performers qualify for the ATP event in Turin and this result leaves Djokovic - the men's game's record 24-time Grand Slam winner - 11th in the standings.

Djokovic admitted he expected to feel "a little rusty" after his win against Frenchman Ugo Humbert on Wednesday, but now faces a fight to make the finals as he is outside the top 10 for the first time since 2018.

Rafael Jodar holds the final qualifying spot in ninth place, because number one Jannik Sinner is injured and will not take part.

Djokovic is 319 points behind Jodar, although he has the opportunity at the Paris Masters in November to move up the rankings.

The Serb is aiming to move ahead of Roger Federer with his 19th appearance at the finals in Turin.

He has won the event a record seven times and has missed the past two editions with injury - but the last time he failed to qualify on merit was in 2017, when his season was affected by injury.

Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have their places confirmed for the showpiece event in Italy from 15-22 November, although American Shelton also surprisingly lost in Basel.

The top seed lost 6-3 6-7 (4-7) 7-6 (7-1) to Swiss wildcard Jerome Kym, who is ranked 222nd in the world.

title: New World Athletics department to cater for running operations, events
article_text:
The World Athletics governing body has launched a new, standalone division to manage its operations and competitions in the world of running.

The Running & Mass Participation department was unveiled earlier this week, to be led by experienced sports governing body executive Jakob Larsen.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The new department will be responsible for World Athletics' substantial portfolio of road running, marathon, cross country, and mountain and trail events and series. In addition, it will oversee regulation, technical and educational services, as well as "the development of new partnerships and opportunities across technology, data, and the wider running industry."

Larsen will work alongside Alessio Punzi to head up this department.

Jon Ridgeon, chief executive at Monaco-headquartered World Athletics, commented: "World Athletics’ research informs us that at least 1 billion people worldwide are runners in some shape or form, making athletics the most-participated sport in the world. Mass participation running possesses the unique power to engage entire communities […] Running is also one of the fastest-growing areas of our sport."

Currently, over 320 events worldwide hold a World Athletics 'road race' label.

This move by World Athletics has been unveiled ahead of the 2026 edition of mass-participation running's iconic TCS New York City Marathon (Sunday, November 1).

Larsen first joined World Athletics in 2020, and has spent the last three years as its head of product research and development.

Before that, he was its competitions and events director.

Prior to joining the global body, meanwhile, he spent time as a joint race director at the Copenhagen Half Marathon, while he has also spent 19 years in total working for the Danish Athletic Federation.

Punzi, meanwhile, has been at World Athletics for just over a decade. Before that, he completed a nine-month project contract at cycling's UCI governing body.

title: Brentford partners with HPE on matchday connectivity
article_text:
Brentford has signed a partnership with Hewlett Packard Enterprise to support the digital fan experience at Gtech Community Stadium.

The agreement follows the deployment of HPE’s networking technology at the Premier League club’s ground, where it provides connectivity across the seating bowl, concourses, hospitality areas and the stadium perimeter. On matchdays, the network is used by supporters, employees, stewards and stadium operations teams.

For fans, the network gives access to the Brentford FC app and club content, and supports interactive activities and competitions during matches. The club is also looking at using the network for loyalty schemes and further supporter engagement.

The same infrastructure runs stadium operations, including digital ticketing, steward devices and health and safety processes. Connected devices give stewards greater visibility of supporters as they enter the ground, and coverage across indoor and outdoor areas supports staff on the move during events.

Fran Jones, Commercial Director at Brentford, said, “We are always looking at how technology can improve the experience for our fans, and connectivity is an important part of that. HPE has given us a reliable foundation across Gtech Community Stadium that supports both our supporters and our teams. It also gives us the flexibility to explore new digital experiences as we continue to evolve the matchday.”

Mark Weeks, Networking Sales Director, UK & Ireland at HPE, said, “Modern stadiums are becoming increasingly digital environments, with technology supporting everything from how fans interact with their clubs to how teams manage a matchday. Our work with Brentford FC shows how a strong foundation can help clubs introduce new services and innovations over time.”

title: Cavs renew with SeatGeek, Whoop reveals investor James as brand ambassador
article_text:
The Cleveland Cavaliers NBA franchise has renewed its long-standing partnership with digital ticketing platform SeatGeek.

The multi-year extension ensures SeatGeek will remain the team’s official ticketing partner.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

SeatGeek has been a partner of the Cavaliers since 2020 and handles ticketing for all events at the team’s 19,432-capacity Rocket Arena home, as well as all properties owned by the Rock Entertainment Group.

This includes all games for the Cavaliers, its NBA G League affiliate, the Cleveland Charge, the American Hockey League’s Cleveland Monsters, and the Cavs Legion NBA2K esports team, as well as concerts and other events at the venue.

Through five games of the 2026-27 NBA season, the Cavaliers have a winning record of three wins and two losses.

The franchise has made the playoffs in each of the past four seasons, including a run to the Eastern Conference Finals last season.

Elsewhere in the basketball world, wearable sports tech brand Whoop has extended and expanded its partnership with former Cavs star LeBron James.

Whoop claims that James, a legend for the Cavs, Miami Heat, and LA Lakers franchises, and arguably the greatest player in NBA history, has worn its tech since 2015.

This new agreement formalizes his role as a global brand ambassador, through which he will appear in global marketing campaigns, content, and activations across Whoop’s social media and digital channels.

James, currently playing for the Philadelphia 76ers in his 24th NBA season, is already a minority stakeholder in the fitness brand.

Earlier in 2026, Whoop was valued at $10.1 billion and attracted $575 million in investment led by investment funds 2PointZero Group, Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), and Mubadala Investment, and including celebrity athlete investors like James, Cristiano Ronaldo, and Rory McIlroy.

title: UNA Sports takes 25% stake in The Curling Group
article_text:
The UNA Sports Group investment firm is taking a stake of around 25% in The Curling Group, the owner of the Grand Slam of Curling series and of the Rock League property.

A deal to that effect has been unveiled today, with UNA leaving a wider investment round that also includes Relay Ventures.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

David Rader, UNA's president and co-founder, and the investment firm's chief executive and managing partner – Del Wright – are both now joining The Curling Group's board.

UNA is set to provide expertise to the curling property on strategy, commercial partnerships, and overall growth initiatives.

Rock League represents the first fully professional curling league.

Rader has commented: "Curling’s audience is growing, getting younger and going global. The TCG team has built the pieces to serve it: a premium event series in the Grand Slam of Curling, a direct line to fans through Rock Channel, and a brand-new league in Rock League. We’re excited to join the board and help build a business that matches the sport’s momentum."

Aside from this latest investment, UNA's portfolio also includes the New York City summer and winter teams from action sports' new X Games League, through a deal unveiled in May.

In addition, the firm has also invested in women's 3-on-3 basketball property Unrivaled.

In general, UNA focuses on acquiring and partnering with global professional sports franchises and platforms.

Nic Sulsky, CEO and co-founder of The Curling Group, added: "UNA’s experience building franchises in emerging leagues, and its team’s prior experience on deals across the NHL, NBA and Formula 1, make them the right partner for our next stage.

and the United States. Five years from now, I want them to see that we’ve changed what the sport can be globally.”

This season has seen The Curling Group sign five-year media rights agreements in Canada with both CBC and Sportsnet, as well as a three-year tie-up with ESPN in the US. These deals cover both the Grand Slam of Curling, and Rock League.

The group also owns Rock Channel, a curling-dedicated media platform and live streaming service, which it launched in late 2024 (at the same time as it acquired the Grand Slam of Curling).

The deal has been announced ahead of the start of the Grand Slam of Curling Masters on November 3, while the first full Rock League season runs across five events between January and April next year.

Rock League features six mixed-gendered global franchises, and made its debut – through a mini-season – in April.

In terms of curling's growing popularity in general, earlier this month the season-opening Co-Op Invitational from The Grand Slam of Curling brought in 38.3 million video views overall – up 415% year-on-year.

title: World Rugby statement: Stability of top-level Samoan rugby safeguarded by governance review
article_text:
Following talks led by World Rugby Chair Brett Robinson and Samoa’s Prime Minister Hon. Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Fosi Schmidt, an action plan has been put in place to ensure the continued participation of the country’s national teams in top-level tournaments.

Differences between the union’s board and management and the Samoan government prompted a governance review, which has resulted in the union’s self-suspension from the World Rugby Council.

Control and jurisdiction of all matters relating to the high-performance rugby programme in Samoa has been transferred instead to the Samoa Association of Sports and National Olympic Committee (SASNOC) with joint oversight from an appointed stewardship group.

Meanwhile, a Samoan-led Independent Review Group, the membership of which shall be agreed by Lakapi Samoa (the Samoan RU) and the Government of Samoa has been appointed, to review all issues pertaining to the governance of Samoan rugby.

Samoa’s men have played at every Rugby World Cup tournament since their debut in 1991, but they only just qualified for the 2027 edition in Australia next year by pocketing the 20th ticket to the tournament via the Final Qualification Tournament.

The team has slipped to an all-time low of 20th in the World Rugby Rankings against a backdrop of off-field problems and has only won one of its first three games in the World Rugby Nations Cup.

Last year, the Samoan women’s team struggled badly at their World Cup, scoring just three points and conceding 225 points after three heavy defeats.

The World Rugby statement reads: “World Rugby, the Government of Samoa, Lakapi Samoa and the Samoa National Olympic Committee have agreed a process to ensure Samoa and its players continue competing at the sport’s highest levels during a governance review. The agreement follows productive meetings in Apia this week led by World Rugby Chair Brett Robinson and Prime Minister of Samoa, Hon. Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Fosi Schmidt.

“The agreed steps address concerns about Lakapi Samoa’s governance and administration raised with World Rugby earlier this year by the Hon. Prime Minister on behalf of the Government. Those concerns, and those of other rugby stakeholders, prompted immediate dialogue between all parties to resolve the issues and agree a way forward.

“All parties agreed that it was imperative that the union’s high-performance programmes remain unaffected, with Samoa’s national teams committed to participating in Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027, the World Rugby Nations Cup, WXV Global Series Challenger and sevens programmes.”

- The self-suspension of Lakapi Samoa from the World Rugby Council. This self-suspension can only be lifted by a future request to the Executive Board of World Rugby and a subsequent recommendation to the World Rugby Council. In any event, the self-suspension shall remain in place during the review processes referenced below.

- Appointment of a Samoan-led Independent Review Group, the membership of which shall be agreed by Lakapi Samoa and the Government of Samoa, to review all issues pertaining to the governance of Samoan rugby.

- A review of Lakapi Samoa’s compliance with World Rugby’s membership criteria by a World Rugby oversight committee.

- Transfer of control and jurisdiction of all matters relating to the high-performance rugby programme in Samoa to the Samoa Association of Sports and National Olympic Committee (SASNOC) with joint oversight from an appointed stewardship group. This group shall be responsible for all matters on and off the field relating to the national teams, including their preparation and participation in global elite competitions such as Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027.

All parties agreed that domestic rugby activities taking place in Samoa shall remain unaffected.

The statement closes by saying: “The proactive support of SASNOC in working closely with World Rugby to safeguard player high-performance pathways and opportunities is greatly appreciated by all stakeholders.”

title: Matchroom's Hearn expected to increase Prem influence
article_text:
Renowned boxing promoter Eddie Hearn is expected to ramp up his influence in rugby union after meeting with Prem bosses in Monaco last week.

Hearn, who runs Matchroom Sport, has made a foray into rugby by signing high-profile players Finn Russell and Henry Pollock to his stable.

And the sports mogul has been backed to make a big impact in the sport by senior figures in the English game.

"[Matchroom] will be a force for good. [Hearn] sees that rugby is on a great trajectory and he's very pro the Prem," said Prem Rugby chief executive Simon Massie-Taylor.

"I think his ambition goes beyond just representing top athletes.

"He doesn't want to be a disruptor. He wants to work with the league, but he definitely wants to agitate for more growth and sees a lot of potential."

Hearn has spoken previously of his desire to "turbo-charge" the profile of rugby union and its players, adding it would be a "stroll in the park" to transform the sport.

"I'd expect him to represent some more of the top stars in the Prem," said Massie-Taylor.

"And so you start to move into other options, whether that's around events, big games, or something specifically commercial around the players across the league.

"I don't think he's there to buy a rugby club, but he could definitely help introduce people to it and partner with that."

Massie-Taylor was speaking around the release of the Prem's second annual financial monitoring report, which revealed that all 10 clubs have passed the financial standards for the 2026/2027 season.

Following the demise of London Irish, Wasps and Worcester, the Prem has tightened up its rules with clubs now required to be more transparent over the state of their finances.

According to the report the financial picture has improved across the league, with revenues up and club losses forecast to reduce by £26.7m, while Newcastle Red Bulls, Exeter Chiefs and Bath Rugby have all secured major external investment over the past 12 months.

However no club is yet in profit, with Saracens and Sale reporting the heaviest losses.

"In the next five years we would expect the vast majority of clubs to move into the black," said Massie-Taylor.

"And for those that don't the losses would be relatively marginal. But I think there will be a situation when clubs move into a more sustainable position, there will be a desire to re-invest.

"So as long as the asset is growing quicker than the aggregate losses, then you have value."

The report reiterates the plan for the Prem to increase from 10 to 12 teams by the 2030/31 season, with expression of interests to be completed in the coming months.

Massie-Taylor confirmed future entrants to the Prem must play at least one season in the second-tier Champ and would also need a large cash advance to purchase a "P-Share", which is thought to be valued at around £20m.

It's understood the Welsh Rugby Union has approached the Prem about the possibility of Welsh sides joining to form an Anglo-Welsh league, and while not shutting the door completely on the prospect, Massie-Taylor said the priority remains to develop clubs in the English system.

"The assumption when we were doing Project Forge [English rugby's strategic plan] was that we were looking to develop English clubs," he added.

title: What Novak Djokovic needs to do at the Paris Masters to qualify for ATP Finals?
article_text:
Novak Djokovic faces an uphill battle to qualify for the ATP Tour Finals after losing to Jan-Lennard Struff at the Basel Open on Thursday.

Despite dropping the first set, Djokovic was unable to hold back the storm as Struff edged out a 6-7 (4), 7-5, 7-6 (5) victory to reach the quarter-finals of the ATP 500 event.

Struff snapped an eight-match losing streak to the 24-time major winner, with Djokovic full of praise for his opponent after their two-hour and 36-minute-long battle.

He told Sportal, “I think it’s just that in the decisive moments, when I had break points, many times in the second and also at the beginning of the third set, he played some incredible shots and incredible points.

“Maybe there were one or two points where I could have been more aggressive, but all credit goes to him.”

After the loss, Djokovic turned his attention to next week’s Paris Masters, where the Serbian will need to score heavily if he wants to qualify for the season-ending event in Turin.

Heading into the business end of the ATP 500 events in Basel and Vienna, Djokovic currently sits 11th in the ATP Tour Race, with 2,890 points to his name.

At present, Rafael Jodar is in the last qualification spot on 3,184 points but his early Basel exit opens the door for the likes of Alex De Minaur and Taylor Fritz to overtake him.

At the time of writing, the ATP Finals qualification cut stands at 3,785 points. For now, there are still five spots available. Here are the current standings below.

Quite simply, if Djokovic wins the Paris Masters, which starts on Monday, he will overtake Jodar in the Race, and that should be enough to secure his place at the ATP Finals.

Those 1,000 points would take him to 3,890 points, which puts him above the qualification cut-off. However, if De Minaur wins Vienna, that takes him to 3,330 points, and if he were to reach the final in Paris, that would catapult him to 3,930 points, just shading out Djokovic.

So even if Djokovic wins in Bercy, he may not qualify. If the likes of De Minaur, Fritz, and Tommy Paul don’t pick up any more points this week and lose in their Paris openers, the Serb will need to reach the semi-finals. That will pocket him 360 points, which would see him overhaul his 319-point deficit to Jodar.

So at the minimum, he needs a semi-final run, and at the maximum, he needs to win the title. However, Djokovic may need some of his rivals to slip up in the French capital.

title: Mitsubishi Electric secures World Cup naming rights and Tour de Ski partnership
article_text:
Mitsubishi Electric has partnered with the International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS), securing title sponsorship of the FIS Nordic Combined World Cup and premium partner status for the 2026–27 FIS Tour de Ski.

The agreement strengthens the Japanese company’s association with international winter sports while supporting the development and visibility of Nordic skiing.

Under the agreement, the Nordic Combined World Cup will carry the name Mitsubishi Electric FIS Nordic Combined World Cup. The company has also become an official premium partner of the FIS Tour de Ski performance by Le Gruyère AOP 2026–27, one of the leading events on the international cross-country skiing calendar.

The partnership will provide Mitsubishi Electric with brand exposure at competition venues, along race courses and during award ceremonies. The 2026–27 Tour de Ski is scheduled to run from January 1–10, 2027, with competitions taking place across France, Germany and Italy.

The agreement comes as FIS seeks to reinforce Nordic Combined, a discipline that brings together ski jumping and cross-country skiing. It also coincides with continued efforts to expand opportunities for women in the sport. The upcoming season will include the first women-only team event in Nordic Combined at a FIS Nordic World Ski Championships, marking a significant milestone for the discipline.

Kazuhiko Tamura, President & CEO of Mitsubishi Electric Europe B.V., said, “We are proud to partner with FIS and support Nordic skiing across a season that brings together world-class competition, progress and ambition. This partnership gives us a meaningful opportunity to connect more closely with the communities in Northern Europe and Scandinavia in which we live and work, while supporting athletes across the Nordic disciplines. We are particularly pleased that the season will include the first women-only Team event in Nordic Combined at a Nordic World Ski Championship, supporting our wider commitment to supporting women in sport.”

Urs Lehman, FIS Secretary General, added, “FIS has made it clear that it is doubling down on Nordic Combined, one of the most traditional and demanding of all snow sports disciplines. To keep following through on this commitment, there is nothing more valuable than counting on a partner like Mitsubishi Electric.”

The agreement gives Mitsubishi Electric a presence across two distinct Nordic skiing properties, combining title sponsorship with event-level visibility and a broader commitment to the sport’s future.

title: SIC seeks five-year Petronas sponsorship extension for Malaysian MotoGP
article_text:
SEPANG: Sepang International Circuit (SIC) hopes Petronas will continue its commitment as title sponsor of the Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (MotoGP) after the current contract expires this year, ensuring the continuity of a strategic partnership that began in 2022.

SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said the circuit hoped discussions between the current title sponsor and MotoGP commercial rights holder Dorna Sports would reach a positive outcome, allowing both parties to continue staging the prestigious race together.

He said that if an agreement was reached, SIC hoped the sponsorship extension would align with Dorna’s five-year contract, which runs until 2031.

“Petronas is a very good brand and highly synonymous with MotoGP. We hope the discussions will produce a positive decision.

“If possible, we want to match the previous contract with Dorna, which is five years,” he told reporters here today.

He was commenting on Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s meeting with MotoGP executive director Carmelo Ezpeleta yesterday, during which Ahmad Zahid, among other things, expressed hope that Petronas would renew its MotoGP sponsorship commitment.

Shafriman said SIC had yet to receive any further updates on Petronas’ intention to continue the sponsorship, stressing that the decision rested entirely with the company.

Petronas became the Malaysian GP title sponsor in 2022, taking over the role from Shell.

Yesterday, Ahmad Zahid said the proposal to ensure Petronas remained the MotoGP title sponsor in the coming years would be discussed with Petronas president and group chief executive officer Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik Tengku Aziz.

title: SponsorUnited: MLB teams combined to generate $2.12B in 2026 sponsorship revenue
article_text:
MLB teams combined to generate $2.12B in sponsorship revenue in 2026, a 7.3% increase from the previous year, according to a report from SponsorUnited. It also represents a 57% increase in MLB team sponsorship value between 2022 ($1.35B) and 2026, with total deals up 17% over that span (3,195 to 3,732).

The average MLB team sponsorship deal size is $590,000, up 5.9% YOY.

Two teams heading to new ballparks led in sponsorship revenue growth: the Rays (33.8% YOY increase) and the Athletics (19.3% YOY increase). The Dodgers, who last year became the first team in North American pro sports to surpass $200M in annual sponsorship revenue (14.5% YOY increase), the White Sox (14.5% YOY increase) and the Mariners (10.2% YOY increase) rounded out the top-five.

Deal count leaders include the Reds (223), Yankees (171), Padres (156), Braves (155) and Astros (151). Sponsorship category leaders include financial ($349M, up 11.92% YOY), beverage ($176M, flat), auto ($155M, flat), insurance ($151M, up 3.62% YOY) and construction/industry ($115M, up 13.19% YOY). There were 632 new brand entrants versus 549 brand exits.

All 30 teams have struck jersey patch sponsorship deals, with the average deal at $8.6M, up 1.3% YOY. The White Sox (CME Group), Rays (Webull) and Giants (Airwallex) generated over $20M combined in sponsorship revenue with their 2026 jersey patch deals, according to a SponsorUnited estimate.

Cal Raleigh (17) has the most player endorsement deals, followed by Julio Rodriguez (16), Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (13), George Springer (10) and Bobby Witt Jr. (nine). SponsorUnited lists Pete Crow-Armstrong (six), Jacob Misiorowski (three), Junior Caminero (eight), Cam Schlittler (zero) and Jordan Walker (one) as players to watch on the endorsement front.

There are 472 active player-brand endorsement deals, down from 627 in 2025. Endorsement retention rates for players are 30% compared to 73.3% for teams, with player deals typically shorter.

title: Welsh rugby player stood down over horror act as ban appeal launched
article_text:
Ebbw Vale second-row Curtis Gregory will not feature for the Steelman this weekend, with the lock currently appealing a ban following his stamp against Llandovery last week.

Gregory was given a straight red card by Craig Evans for a stamp on the leg of Drovers captain Joe Powell. While a hefty ban was expected for the second-row, nothing had been announced by the Welsh Rugby Union prior to Ebbw Vale naming their team for Saturday's Super Rygbi Cymru match against Cardiff on Saturday at the Arms Park.

In some instances at the lower level, a disciplinary hearing can take place more than a week after the initial incident - meaning some players could be free to play in any matches before a ban is handed out.

However, Gregory will not play - with it understood he was in front of a disciplinary panel this week.

It is not yet clear how long Gregory has been banned for, but as he is currently appealing the ban, it means he is unable to play.

As such, Saturday's top-of-the-table clash in the Welsh capital will count towards whatever ban Gregory is eventually handed.

Footage of the incident has been spread far and wide, after Gregory stamped on Powell's outstretched leg while the Llandovery player was on the floor.

Thankfully, Powell escaped without injury.

Referee Craig Evans stopped play immediately in the 35th minute, saying: "We have a stamp by this player.

"I did ask the question if anything aggravated it.

"My AR (assistant referee) didn't see anything. It's a stamp on the leg. Red card. Permanent."

The game was being shown live by S4C and replays of the incident drew groans from the Welsh language commentators.

Online discourse has seen some call for a severe punishment - although that should be weighed up against the fact that footage of the incident has perhaps travelled further than anyone could have imagined.

title: Rugby Union: Eddie Hearn expected to up Prem influence
article_text:
Renowned boxing promoter Eddie Hearn is expected to ramp up his influence in rugby union after meeting with Prem bosses in Monaco last week.

Hearn, who runs Matchroom Sport, has made a foray into rugby by signing high-profile players Finn Russell and Henry Pollock to his stable.

And the sports mogul has been backed to make a big impact in the sport by senior figures in the English game.

"[Matchroom] will be a force for good. [Hearn] sees that rugby is on a great trajectory and he's very pro the Prem," said Prem Rugby chief executive Simon Massie-Taylor.

"I think his ambition goes beyond just representing top athletes.

"He doesn't want to be a disruptor. He wants to work with the league, but he definitely wants to agitate for more growth and sees a lot of potential."

Hearn has spoken previously of his desire to "turbo-charge" the profile of rugby union and its players, adding it would be a "stroll in the park" to transform the sport.

"I'd expect him to represent some more of the top stars in the Prem," said Massie-Taylor.

"And so you start to move into other options, whether that's around events, big games, or something specifically commercial around the players across the league.

"I don't think he's there to buy a rugby club, but he could definitely help introduce people to it and partner with that."

Massie-Taylor was speaking around the release of the Prem's second annual financial monitoring report, which revealed that all 10 clubs have passed the financial standards for the 2026/2027 season.

Following the demise of London Irish, Wasps and Worcester, the Prem has tightened up its rules with clubs now required to be more transparent over the state of their finances.

According to the report the financial picture has improved across the league, with revenues up and club losses forecast to reduce by £26.7m, while Newcastle Red Bulls, Exeter Chiefs and Bath Rugby have all secured major external investment over the past 12 months.

However no club is yet in profit, with Saracens and Sale reporting the heaviest losses.

"In the next five years we would expect the vast majority of clubs to move into the black," said Massie-Taylor.

"And for those that don't the losses would be relatively marginal. But I think there will be a situation when clubs move into a more sustainable position, there will be a desire to re-invest.

"So as long as the asset is growing quicker than the aggregate losses, then you have value."

The report reiterates the plan for the Prem to increase from 10 to 12 teams by the 2030/31 season, with expression of interests to be completed in the coming months.

Massie-Taylor confirmed future entrants to the Prem must play at least one season in the second-tier Champ and would also need a large cash advance to purchase a "P-Share", which is thought to be valued at around £20m.

It's understood the Welsh Rugby Union has approached the Prem about the possibility of Welsh sides joining to form an Anglo-Welsh league, and while not shutting the door completely on the prospect, Massie-Taylor said the priority remains to develop clubs in the English system.

"The assumption when we were doing Project Forge [English rugby's strategic plan] was that we were looking to develop English clubs," he added.

"That's where we see a lot of potential, whether that's clubs within the Champ, clubs that maybe are outside the Champ and in the English system elsewhere, and previous clubs [for example a reborn Wasps or London Irish].

"So we're putting a lot of resource and attention in developing them. It wasn't a debate at the time around Welsh clubs."

title: Kieran Hardy: Ospreys and Wales scrum-half faces World Cup fitness race
article_text:
Wales scrum-half Kieran Hardy faces a race to be fit for next year's World Cup in Australia.

Hardy, 30, has had surgery this week after suffering a serious knee injury in the United Rugby Championship (URC) victory against Dragons at Rodney Parade.

Ospreys head coach Mark Jones has confirmed Hardy will miss the rest of the season but hopes Hardy can be fit in time for the World Cup which starts in October 2027.

"It is a serious knee injury which has needed surgery which tells you its extent," said Jones.

"It was a to major ligament of the knee and he has got some other bits and pieces that needed rectifying as well.

"We are definitely not going to see him this season, we just hope he has a good rehabilitation, there are no kinks in the road and everything goes to plan.

"We will be crossing everything that he is around for the start of the next season and his availability with the World Cup on the horizon."

Hardy has been a regular Wales deputy for Tomos Williams, while Ospreys team-mate Reuben Morgan-Williams and the uncapped Dragons number nine Che Hope have also been named in Steve Tandy's side for the Nations Championship in November.

Hardy has never played a World Cup game but was called up to the squad in the tournament in France as injury cover in 2023.

"That will be his target but you have to go with the speed the body lets you," said Jones.

"You have to have goals when you are out for a lengthy period and what better target than playing for your country at a World Cup.

"That is an awesome goal that will keep him on track. He is a great professional and he will apply himself.

"It is a huge carrot, and until somebody tells him that is not achievable, that is what he will be going for."

title: World No. 1 An Se-young Wins, Ranking Points Unchanged
article_text:
[OSEN=Ko Sung-hwan Reporter] It is because she has won too many titles. 'World No. 1' An Se-young, 24 years old, Samsung Life Insurance, failed to add a single point to her Badminton World Federation (BWF) world ranking points despite winning two consecutive tournaments.

Indonesian outlet 'Sumbawa News' reported on the 29th (Korean time), "An Se-young dominates on the court, but her world ranking points have not increased," adding, "An Se-young recently won the Denmark Open and France Open, both Super 750 tournaments, consecutively. However, her BWF world ranking points have remained at 122,287 since October 6."

The outlet explained, "An Se-young earned 11,000 points for each tournament victory, totaling 22,000 points. However, her world ranking points did not increase. This is because the BWF’s world ranking system reflects only the top 10 tournament results achieved in the past 52 weeks."

An Se-young recently swept the Denmark Open and France Open held in Europe. On the 18th, she defeated Akane Yamaguchi (Japan) 2-1 (21-23, 21-14, 21-18) in the Denmark Open final to claim the title. A week later, she overcame Pusarla Venkata Sindhu (India) 2-1 (16-21, 21-11, 21-12) in the France Open final to secure her third consecutive title there.

An Se-young, who added two more championship trophies in quick succession, achieved her 10th title of the season by defending her France Open crown.

Notably, An Se-young is on a remarkable 50-match winning streak. Since her loss to Wang Zhiyi (China) in the All England Open final in March, she has not lost a single match. Her record this year stands at 66 wins and 1 loss, with a win rate of 98.51%. She has lost only once in 67 matches.

Despite writing new history daily, An Se-young’s world ranking points remain stagnant. As of the 27th, she remained at 122,287 points, retaining the No. 1 spot in the women’s singles world rankings—the same score as before her Denmark and France Open victories.

The reason lies in the BWF’s unique ranking system. The BWF reflects only the top 10 tournament results with the highest points earned in the past 52 weeks. Even if a player wins multiple tournaments, the points are not simply accumulated.

For example, newly earned points can only increase the total world ranking points if they exceed the lowest score among the existing top 10 tournaments. Otherwise, no additional points are added, even if the player wins.

An Se-young is in this exact situation. She had already secured such high points in her top 10 tournaments that the 11,000 points from her Super 750 tournament victories could not replace her existing records.

Sumbawa News noted, "The points from the Denmark Open and France Open have not yet been included in her top 10 tournament records. This is because there are no lower scores in her existing records that can be replaced by the newly earned points."

An Se-young had already accumulated high points from other Super 750 tournaments, such as the India Open, Singapore Open, and China Masters. Therefore, the points from the Denmark and France Opens were insufficient to displace her existing records.

An Se-young’s world ranking points last increased on October 6. She achieved back-to-back gold medals in the women’s singles at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in late September.

However, even then, her world ranking points increased by only 1,000. Although she earned 12,000 points for winning the Asian Games women’s singles, her total world ranking points rose from 121,287 to 122,287—an increase of just 1,000.

Ultimately, An Se-young has built such an overwhelming record that even her tournament victories struggle to add to her world ranking points. For a typical player, winning a Super 750 tournament would significantly boost their ranking, but for An Se-young, such victories are insufficient to replace her existing points.

Of course, her No. 1 ranking remains unshaken. Thanks to her accumulated remarkable results, she continues to hold the top spot despite her consecutive tournament wins not affecting her total points.

An Se-young’s challenge is far from over. Last year, she set a single-season record with 11 tournament wins. This year, she completed her 10th title before October even ended, putting her in direct competition with her own record. If she adds one more title, she will tie last year’s record, and another victory will etch a new history in badminton singles.

title: Brooks Koepka Takes A Shot At Bryson DeChambeau Over Masters Row With Rory McIlroy

We thought his beef with Bryson DeChambeau was a thing of the past, but Brooks Koepka couldn't resist taking a shot at his old sparring partner.

This time with reference to his 2025 Masters Sunday showdown with Rory McIlroy, when DeChambeau complained that the eventual Green Jacket winner didn't talk to him all day.

Koepka's not known as a huge talker either, just one reason why his personality often grinds up against the more outgoing DeChambeau, so was firmly on McIlroy's side.

Speaking to Dan Rapaport, five-time Major champion Koepka joked about DeChmbeau that "I don't think many people want to talk to him regardless".

DeChambeau was keen to engage with McIlroy on that Sunday at Augusta National, but the Northern Irishman brushed him off, later explaining: "We’re trying to win the Masters. I’m not going to try to be his best mate out there.”

Koepka is in the McIlroy camp on this one and, unsurprisingly given how he went about winning his five Majors, would not have been chatting away while trying to win one of the biggest prizes in golf.

“I wouldn’t have spoken to Rory, and I don’t think he would have spoken to me and it would have been totally fine,” Koepka told the Dan on Golf YouTube show.. “I’m not a big talker. I’ll talk a little bit, maybe the first couple of holes.

“I fully understand it. I don’t feel bad. It is what it is. Some guys don’t talk. It’s okay. It’s their job. They get to do what they want."

"I mean, he lives in his own world," Koepka added. "I mean, I don't think many people want to talk to him regardless."

title: Shorts: Maro Itoje, ITV, UK Sport
article_text:
Nutrition brand AG1 has signed Maro Itoje, captain of England and Saracens and of the 2025 British & Irish Lions, as a member and athlete ambassador on a two-year deal.

The partnership launches with a campaign titled “The foundation of a captain”, which follows Itoje’s daily life across rugby, his cultural interests and his family. The first film, “Take One”, has been released through Itoje’s and AG1’s social media channels. Further films will follow, including an edition of AG1’s “Morning Person” format, along with longform press, podcast content and a UK events programme over the coming months.

According to AG1, Itoje was already a daily user of the product before the deal. He was invited to a brand dinner earlier this year hosted by Chief Executive Officer Kat Cole, International President Tim Harrington and long-term partner Dr Rangan Chatterjee.

The agreement adds to AG1’s existing work in rugby, where it partners the England, Ireland and Australia national teams. The brand also partners Swansea City and works with athletes including three-time world surfing champion Mick Fanning.

Away from rugby, Itoje founded the Akoje Gallery, which champions African, Caribbean and diasporic artists. He holds a politics degree from SOAS, University of London, and an MBA from Warwick Business School. He also funds education for disadvantaged children through the Pearl Fund and hosts the podcast Power & Purpose.

Tim Harrington, International President of AG1, said, “Maro embodies exactly what we look for in a partner – someone who lives our product, not just endorses it. His story, on and off the pitch, is proof that consistency compounds. We’re proud to help him tell it.”

Itoje said, “Whether it’s rugby, art, or philanthropy – I’ve always believed success is built through consistency, by doing all the little things well, time and time again. AG1 gives me the boost to do that in all the important areas of my work and life.”

ITV has been named official broadcaster of Netball Aid, the celebrity charity netball event returning to the Utilita Arena Birmingham on 15th November.

The broadcaster will film the preview, match and post-match review for a 90-minute show on ITVX, and will air a 30-minute highlights programme on ITV4.

This year’s event, the second edition after its launch in 2025, will raise money for Shelter, the housing charity, which campaigns in particular for vulnerable women and children.

The celebrity line-up includes Olympic champions Dame Denise Lewis, Dame Laura Kenny and Jade Jones, former England rugby captain Chris Robshaw, 2026 Apprentice winner Karishma, Capital Breakfast host Sian Welby and 2026 Love Island contestant Ellie Chadwick.

Three matches will be played across the day. The programme opens with an Invictus match supporting the Invictus Games Foundation. England Men’s Netball then play the Birmingham Basketball Rockets in Battle of the Balls, marking 100 years of netball, before the celebrity match starts at 3pm.

Alison Akinrinlola, Co-Founder of Netball Aid, said, “We are delighted to have ITV on board as our official broadcaster. ITV is home to some of the biggest moments in British sport and entertainment, and to have a partner of that calibre championing Netball Aid is a dream come true.“

“Their team has shared our passion from the very first conversation and we couldn’t ask for a better partner to bring Netball Aid into homes across the country.”

Scott Smith, Chief Financial Officer at Six Nations Rugby, has been appointed to the UK Sport Board by the Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport. His four-year term begins on 1st November.

Smith has sat on UK Sport’s Group Audit and Risk Committee for the past four years. On the board, he will bring finance, governance and commercial strategy experience as the organisation continues its 10-year strategic plan for Olympic and Paralympic sport and major events.

At Six Nations Rugby, he plays a leading role in the organisation’s strategic and commercial development. He previously held senior finance roles at the England and Wales Cricket Board and the America’s Cup, working on major international events, commercial growth strategies and organisational change programmes.

His non-executive and advisory roles include positions with Racecourse Media Group, Archery GB and the EURO 2028 Oversight Group. He is a Fellow Chartered Accountant in both the UK and Australia.

Professor Nick Webborn, Chair of UK Sport, said, “Scott has already made a valuable contribution through our Group Audit and Risk Committee, and his insight will further strengthen the Board as we continue to support Olympic and Paralympic success and deliver impact through major sporting events across the UK. I look forward to working with him in the years ahead.”

Scott Smith, Chief Financial Officer at Six Nations Rugby, said, “UK Sport plays a vital role not only in delivering success on the world stage, but also in building a strong, sustainable high performance sporting system for future generations. With the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games taking place in my home city, there is an added personal significance to the journey ahead.”

Scottish Rugby has appointed Dave Butcher as permanent Head Coach of Scotland Women. He has led the team on an interim basis since the summer, including through the WXV Global Series.

Butcher joined Scotland Women as Forwards Coach for the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations, before stepping up as interim Head Coach. His most recent role before that was Assistant Coach (Forwards) with Canada, who reached the final of the 2025 Women’s Rugby World Cup.

title: X Games appoints Asencio as commercial head
article_text:
X Games, the iconic action sports property, has hired experienced sports executive Paul Asencio to lead its commercial operations as chief revenue officer (CRO).

In the role, he will lead global partnerships, sponsorship sales, and commercial revenue strategy for X Games and the new X Games League (XGL), reporting to chief executive Jeremy Bloom.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Asencio has more than 25 years of commercial experience across several major sports properties, including the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) mixed martial arts promotion, the Williams Formula 1 motor racing team, the New York Mets Major League Baseball franchise, and international e-commerce and merchandising giant Fanatics.

He spent more than five years leading sponsorship as senior vice president of global partnerships at UFC, before serving as CRO of Williams Racing, where he oversaw commercial and marketing operations.

Asencio spent 17 years with the Mets in multiple roles, including senior vice president of corporate partnerships, sales and services, followed by two years as vice president of venue business development at Fanatics.

Most recently, he served as executive vice president of global partnerships at sports media and marketing technology firm Playfly Sports.

Bloom said: “We've spent the last two years building an entirely new model for action sports, and the momentum behind X Games is as strong as ever. We've launched a professional sports league with eight teams and a growing global footprint. Now it's about turning that momentum into a sustainable, scalable global business.

“Paul helped drive global commercial growth at UFC and Formula 1, two of the biggest growth stories in sports. He knows how to build high-performing teams, create meaningful partnerships, and turn passionate fandom into long-term value.”

The X Games format was transformed from standalone events into a professional team-based league, with the new concept announced in September 2025, which organizers hope will provide athletes with more structure, visibility, and earning opportunities. Following this year’s inaugural summer season, it plans to expand to a winter competition in 2027.

X Games has secured ownership groups for six of eight inaugural XGL clubs: XC New York (winter and summer), XC Los Angeles and XC São Paulo summer clubs, along with winter clubs XC Golden State and XC Park City.

MoonPay, which was named as X Games title sponsor in January, holds the options for the final two clubs – XC Tokyo (summer) and XC Whistler (winter). Should the option expire, the franchises will be put on the market.

The first XGL summer season took place earlier this year, featuring three stops in Sacramento, California (June 26 to 28) and Chiba, Japan (July 4 and 5), with the season ending with the New Orleans Championship.

The competition is claimed to have reached 18.3 million U.S. television viewers, up 78.5% year over year, with 7.5 million viewers tuning into multiple stops.

The X Games League’s first winter season will be held next year with three stops, including Aspen, Colorado (January 29 to 31), Calgary, Canada (February 19 to 21), and Ruka, Finland (April 9 to 11), which will serve as the championship event.

The X Games League held its first winter athlete draft on September 16 in Los Angeles in preparation for next year’s inaugural season, which will feature skiing and snowboarding disciplines.

Alongside MoonPay, XGL now features a broad roster of big-name sponsors led by founding partner Monster Energy, the energy drinks company, with the league securing an automotive partner, Jeep, betting and streaming partners Stake and Kick.com, technology partners Amazon, Google Cloud, and Anker, and several food and drink partners in BeatBox Beverages, 805 Beer, Pacifico, Kraken Rum, High Noon, Factor, and TinCup Whiskey.

Earlier this month, ticketing and entertainment tech provider Fever was brought in as its official ticketing platform.

Other official partners include the US Army, Polaris, Bobcat, and iHeartRadio.

title: ‘They make me look good’: Bella Vogel puts team first after historic World Rugby nomination
article_text:
Jack Hanratty already knew that Bella Vogel was a talent when he first called her into Eagles camp. Two-footed kickers do not grow on trees. It was when the 19-year-old sang he knew she was a special player.

This year has been the year of Vogel. On Friday, the 19-year-old will make her 10th Test appearance of 2026 when the USA take on the Red Roses. Ahead of the fixture, she was nominated for World Rugby Women’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year, becoming the first Eagle to receive the recognition. She could even have the award in her hands by full-time at Sports Illustrated Stadium.

“From day one, Bella commanded the room,” Hanratty said. “We use the field as different music genres. In the middle is disco, which is the equivalent of Emilie Bydwell’s street ball – it’s a little bit more fluid. We call it a ‘just say yes’ mentality.

“I was getting the players to tell me what songs represented that. Country is a little more structured and we have that for when we need to be more structured. Then we have our rock and out mosh when we’re in their area.

“Bella was 19 in the first camp, she was the first voice to say, ‘It’s kind of like this disco song’. I didn’t know it, I said, ‘Oh sing it, Bella’. In front of 30 players she hadn’t met before, at 19 years of age, stood up and sang. That was the moment I thought: this is a new era.”

Ever-present for the Eagles since making her debut against the Black Ferns in Pacific Four Series action in April, Vogel’s kicking and distribution has been key to the USA’s current five game win streak.

Dating back to their July victory over South Africa, the USA have won five consecutive matches, including all four of their WXV Global Series fixtures in September and October. Last time out the Eagles were 54-24 winners against Italy in Nashville, Tennessee. The hosts scored eight tries at Geodis Park. All eight tries were scored by forwards, Vogel converted seven.

Two days later and her nomination for Breakthrough Player of the Year was confirmed. Vogel was quick to share the credit.

“I keep getting told, ‘Don’t let your head get too big’ and all that,” she smiled. “I could not [have been nominated] without the team. They make me look good.

‘I give the ball to Freda [Tafuna] and she runs through 10 people. That’s kind of just how our team works. You need your whole team to win an award.”

For the Eagles, Vogel’s nomination is also recognition of a programme beginning to attract attention. Their five-match winning streak has certainly helped.

“It’s an incredible individual accolade,” Hanratty said. “For a number of years, at times there has been talent in this programme that maybe didn’t get international recognition. Sometimes you can feel that.

“There were players in the room who were probably those athletes who deserved a bit more recognition. You could feel the energy and happiness towards one of our own.”

title: 'Has he got dementia?': Pro blasts Sergio Garcia over LIV exit, Euro return
article_text:
On Thursday, Sergio Garcia made it official: he was leaving LIV Golf to rejoin the DP World Tour, with hopes of parlaying that into a PGA Tour return.

The irony of Garcia’s statement, in which he claimed he was “proud” to call the DP World Tour “home” again, was apparent to many who read it. You can count DP World Tour pro Eddie Pepperell among them.

Shortly after Garcia’s announcement, Pepperell sharply criticized Garcia in a strongly-worded social media post of his own.

Garcia is one of the greatest European players of all time. He’s accumulated 16 DP World Tour wins in his career, and he starred on a series of winning European Ryder Cup teams.

But in 2022, he chose to abandon the PGA and DP World Tours in favor of big paydays at LIV Golf. He was suspended by the DP World Tour and later resigned his membership.

And he wasn’t exactly judicious about the split. That year, he ranted to the Telegraph, “This tour is s—, you’re all f—, should have taken the Saudi money,” after the DP World Tour fined LIV players and temporarily banned them from certain events.

And that’s the reason the tone Garcia chose to employ in his DP World Tour return announcement did not sit well with Pepperell.

Pepperell took to X, quote-tweeted Garcia’s own post, and let him have it.

“This has to be Sergio trolling us? Surely. Elite level s—housery, this. Or has he got dementia?” Pepperell asked on X.

A few hours later, Pepperell followed his original post with another, in which he acknowledged that Garcia brings more value to the DP World Tour than he does.

“To be clear, I think Sergio Garcia is still a wonderful player. He was my favourite golfer growing up, ahead of Tiger. And I can see the value he still brings, ahead of me certainly,” Pepperell wrote.

But he wasn’t walking back his point. He continued by declaring that Sergio’s announcement displayed a “stunning” lack of awareness, given his previous criticism of the DP World Tour.

“But his statement today shows a remarkable lack of self awareness,” Pepperell wrote. “Like, a stunning amount.”

Pepperell has been an outspoken critic of LIV Golf for years, but he’s also been remarkably consistent over that time. His primary concern about LIV was how it could negatively impact the DP World Tour.

Back in 2022, LIV Golf’s first season, Pepperell told GOLF’s Dylan Dethier that he’d never join LIV and suggested LIV was actively trying to destroy the DP World Tour.

“It’s like they’re trying to deal the PGA Tour and DP World Tour a slow death by a thousand paper cuts,” Pepperell said at the time.

He’s also worried about how his own career will be affected by a large group of former LIV pros playing the DP World Tour next year.

In a blog post last week, Pepperell wrote that if returning LIV Golf pros were to take his own spots in DP World Tour events, it “would feel like an absolute betrayal.”

But he also acknowledged that the DP World Tour needs star power to aid its dire financial situation. So, while he’s OK with big stars getting special invites, he thinks most LIV Golf pros should have to earn their way back through Q-School.

It’s important to note that none of this is hypothetical for Pepperell. The two-time winner made it through Q-School last season to reclaim his DP World Tour card. This year, he sits in 101st in the Race to Dubai standings, which means his status for next season is at risk.

He’s also not alone in his opinion. Earlier this month, six-time DP World Tour winner Joost Luiten criticized the DP World Tour for allowing LIV pros to return without going through Q-School in an interview with Today’s Golfer.

“[The DP World Tour] should make it harder for guys to come back. Four years ago they didn’t give a s— about the DP World Tour. They made a decision to go after the money. And now all of a sudden, the money is gone and they want to come back and act like nothing happened. I don’t think that’s right,” Luiten told Today’s Golfer.

He continued: “Why give them invites? If I apply for an invite if I’m not in a tournament, I’m not going to get it because it’s all going to the LIV guys. There’s only a certain amount of invites. Invites should be for young talent coming through and not guys that took the piss against this tour and now they want to come back and they get invites. I’m not a big fan of that.”

title: Goldman Sachs Thinks the Sports Boom Isn’t Going Anywhere
article_text:
Within most media companies, sports remain core to their larger content strategy. Premium entertainment isn’t going anywhere, of course, but if you ask Ted Sarandos or Mike Cavanagh or Josh D’Amaro about their content mix, sports will be at the center of it.

“These events break through,” Sarandos said on the company’s last earnings call. “They drive new membership, they add fuel to our ad revenues.”

It’s with that backdrop that Goldman Sachs is releasing a new report focused on sports investing … and the bank is predicting that the sports economy is only going to go up from here.

“We increasingly hear from our clients a continuation of a theme that started with our first paper two years ago, which is this really high level of interest in participating in this explosion that we’re seeing in the sports ecosystem,” says Goldman Sachs partner Nicole Pullen Ross. “When you think about the trajectory of growth within sports, our expectation is that we’ll see growth within the sports ecosystem grow to you know over $600 billion by 2030, that’s 44 percent growth.”

Indeed, the new Goldman report notes a number of things contributing to that explosive growth, from continually rising media rights deals (the bank estimates global sports media rights will hit $67 billion this year); institutional capital buying into teams; and all the ancillary opportunities around entertainment and live events and IP.

“Streaming is now 20 percent of the market for media rights and those contributions of how advertisers are thinking about reaching the consumer in a real-time way is one of the drivers of what we’re seeing,” Ross says. “We’re very analytical in terms of thinking about the value and what the data suggests. One of the things that we saw was the expectation that media rights growth would continue, and the participation was becoming much broader in terms of in terms of the value of the consumer and that live entertainment part of the formula.”

Goldman also dug into some more sector-wide (and in some cases economywide) trends: Institutional investors are buying into teams as league change their roles to give owners more liquidity, and sports team owners, like many business owners, are exploring how artificial intelligence can improve efficiency and create more personalized fan experiences.

But the report also digs into the ancillary opportunities in sports, particularly around athlete-centric brands (athlete-led studios and consumer brands, etc) shortform content, and opportunities like VR tickets to games.

“In an increasingly fragmented media landscape, sports owners are leveraging the power of storytelling to capture and retain a fan base with an increasingly short attention span,” the report states. “Rather than relying solely on traditional broadcasts, they use narrative-driven content to sustain the appeal of live games while capturing younger demographics.”

“When you consider the brands that the athletes have and the longevity of their lives post-career, there is an opportunity one for the athlete to want to invest in their brand and those relationships while they’re still playing, but also the opportunity for them to transition that into areas of focus for their business interests,” Ross says. “So the creativity is around how can we make the athlete more relatable? How can we get more fans to engage? Particularly the younger audience, and how can we use technology as a way to do that? Some of the shortform engagement is an example of that, and so that creativity around making additional ways available to increase engagement and participation is one of the things that we heard from clients and the creativity that they’re using to to make sure that they are having points of differentiated connectivity across their across their attendee base. ultimately, teams want to win, owners want to win.”
