Former Wales and Lions international dies as club pay tribute
article_text:
Cardiff RFC have announced the sad passing of former Wales and British Lions international Keri Jones.

Eighty-one-year-old Jones died on Thursday, October 29.

He joined Cardiff in 1965 and was capped five times by Wales, as well as representing the Barbarians. He toured South Africa with the Lions in 1968 before switching codes and joining Wigan the same year.

In league he was capped twice by Great Britain and appeared at the 1970 Rugby League World Cup.

He was also a talented athlete, representing Great Britain at the 1966 Commonwealth Games in Kingston, Jamaica, as a sprinter.

Cardiff RFC said in a statement: "The club is sad to report that Keri Jones passed away on the morning of 29th October at the age of 81.

"Keri attended Ystalyfera Grammar School and played on the wing for both Neath and Cardiff College of Education before joining Cardiff RFC in 1965.

"However, after only two games for the Blue & Blacks he took a sabbatical from rugby to concentrate on athletics and won a place in the Welsh Commonwealth Games team that went to Jamaica in 1966, running in the 100 yards, 220 yards and sprint relay races.

"Keri returned to rugby union in the 1966-67 and 1967-68 seasons playing a further 58 games and scoring 30 tries for the club. Keri was capped by Wales in five internationals and also played for Barbarians. Keri toured South Africa with the British & Irish Lions in 1968 before signing professional forms for Wigan RLFC later that year.

"As a professional, Keri went on to win two Great Britain caps playing against France and New Zealand in the 1970 Rugby League World Cup which was held in England.

"In retirement, Keri was a long-standing member of the Former Players Association and attended a number of our breakfast gatherings before experiencing ill-health earlier this year.

"We send our sincere condolences to Keri’s wife, Andrea, and their two daughters Lynne & Elen, at this sad time."

Neath RFC, one Jones' other former clubs, also paid tribute.

"A product of Ystalyfera Grammar School, sprint champion Keri made his first-class rugby debut for Neath in a 6-nil win over Maesteg in September 1964 and played for Cardiff College of Education before joining Cardiff RFC.

"He was a member of the Welsh Commonwealth Games team that went to Jamaica in 1966, running in the 100 yards, 220 yards and sprint relay races before returning to rugby union and won his first cap for Wales against New Zealand in 1967 (Brian Thomas propped).

"He played in all four of Wales’ ‘Five Nations’ games that season, represented the Barbarians and toured South Africa with the British Lions in 1968 before joining Wigan RL going on to represent Great Britain.

"Neath RFC’s condolences go to his family and friends."

title: English-born star set to be picked for Six Nations rivals

title: Lions star cleared after accusation as Finn Russell helps exciting Wales talent
article_text:
Here are your rugby headlines for Friday, October 30.

British and Irish Lions star Tadhg Furlong has been cleared of foul play following an allegation that he grabbed an opponent's groin during Leinster's victory over Munster.

The Ireland prop was cited following an incident involving Munster back-rower Gavin Coombes during Leinster's 24-18 win at the Aviva Stadium.

Coombes raised the allegation with referee Andrew Brace during the first half of the contest, prompting television match official Colin Stanley to review the incident. However, the TMO was unable to find conclusive video evidence of any wrongdoing.

Despite that, Furlong was subsequently cited under World Rugby Law 9.27, which states that "a player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals".

The 33-year-old, who has toured with the British and Irish Lions on three occasions, faced a disciplinary hearing on Thursday.

However, the independent panel unanimously dismissed the complaint.

In its findings, the committee said it had "unanimously concluded the citing complaint against the player should be dismissed, on the basis that he did not commit an act of foul play contrary to Law 9.27".

The panel also made clear that it accepted Coombes had provided "an honest account of his recollection of events surrounding the incident", despite finding that Furlong had not committed an act of foul play.

The decision means the experienced tighthead prop will face no disciplinary sanction and is free to return to action.

It also comes as a boost to Ireland ahead of their upcoming Nations Championship fixtures, with Furlong now available for selection for home matches against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa next month.

He will also be eligible to feature in Ireland's finals weekend fixture at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium.

Louie Hennessey says he's benefited from the experience of climbing through the pecking order at Bath - and working alongside Scotland star Finn Russell.

The versatile 22-year-old is likely to be jostling with the likes of Max Llewellyn, Joe Hawkins and the uncapped Aneurin Owen in Steve Tandy's Wales midfield options.

However, having faced a similar battle for contention at Bath with the likes of Ollie Lawrence, Max Ojomoh and Cameron Redpath, he says he feels well placed to make his mark.

"The level that they operate at and what they do on the training field and off it has been great for my development."

Hennessey also says his experience of working so closely with Scotland star Russell has similarly been a huge benefit.

"It's the speed of thought with Finn," he said. "As a youngster coming through I trained on the other side and defended against him, reacting to stuff and trying to think two steps ahead."

Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl has admitted it is disappointing to be playing a Welsh derby this weekend without a number of Wales internationals.

His side travel to Swansea on Saturday night to take on the Ospreys at St Helen's, with six Wales squad members unavailable for selection. As for their opponents, they are without four Wales internationals.

Cardiff have been boosted by Wales releasing Josh Adams back to them, with the wing in need of minutes ahead of the Nations Championship next month.

"Josh has only played close to 100 minutes and if you are to look at Test match preparation you probably need almost double that, so it makes sense," said van Zyl.

He added: "I would say that you want to see derbies with full squads and both teams being able to select whoever they want.

"It's in the schedule and unfortunately there are priorities with Wales. We lose a few and they lose a few, which will test the squads and lead to opportunities.

"There were fewer players available for us but we are excited with the group of players that we have named for what will be a spicy derby."

Franco Smith admits he was disappointed with Roddy Grant’s conduct, which ultimately led to the assistant coach being sacked from his role at Glasgow Warriors.

A statement on Tuesday confirmed Grant had left Scotstoun following an 'internal process'.

No further details have been released about the circumstances of Grant's departure, and while Smith wouldn’t comment on the disciplinary process involved, he stressed the importance of the club's culture and ingrained values.

“Look, the process was followed and we're just going to stick to the task and carry on each week," said Smith.

"Obviously we’re disappointed with everything that happened, but that's that. I think the club dealt with it and we're now heading on to the next thing. That is the way we've approached it.”

Asked if he felt let down by Grant, he added: “Look, we're a tight ship here and everybody knows exactly what my values are and where we stand and how we do things here. The culture of the club has been tried and tested over the last five years, and it comes up flying. That is what I'm proud of.

“This incident didn't influence anything that we did or do or want to become, or want to do, and the type of messaging that we give to the players. So, no, I think we weren't disrupted.

“Again, I think we wanted to give another person an opportunity to be involved in this environment and grow their coaching career. It's not what we can get, it's what we can give, and that was the approach.”

title: Australia's best rugby union player promises better after winning John Eales Medal
article_text:
McReight joined great Australian opensides George Smith, Phil Waugh, David Pocock and Michael Hooper in taking home the prestigious award, which is decided by a ballot of Wallabies players after each test.

"It's a tremendous honour. I think all you ever want is to be respected by your fellow mates and it means a lot," the 27-year-old told reporters after receiving the award late on Thursday.

"But here's just the beginning for me. I really think I'm getting a lot better ... So I'm eager for next year.

"I'm eager to continue this form and playing for Australia, because I love this country and I love this team."

McReight, who was the first Queensland player since Chris Latham in 2006 to claim the prize, said he was looking forward to seeing the Wallabies continue to improve over the next 12 months heading into the World Cup on home soil.

"We know we can be more detailed, take the learnings, and continue to grow," he said.

"Like, everyone's seen our performances. When we play well, we're a great side. We just got to keep getting better.

"You don't play the game for these honours, right?" McReight added. "You play to win as a team. And all I care about is winning and having a beer in the sheds with my mates."

In other awards, inside centre Faitala Moleka was named Wallaroos Player of the Year, while McReight's versatile backline teammate Jock Campbell was named Australia's best in Super Rugby Pacific.

title: Medvedev returns to the Nitto ATP Finals
Alcaraz repels Basilashvili’s 4 set points in Vienna, books QF spot
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz earned a victory of two starkly contrasting halves to reach his 60th tour-level quarter-final on Thursday at the Erste Bank Open.

The No. 3 player in the PIF ATP Rankings, Alcaraz held off a second-set resurgence from Nikoloz Basilashvili to claim a 6-1, 7-6(11) triumph in Vienna. Basilashvili entered the clash having won 14 of his past 17 matches and recovered from a difficult start to hand Alcaraz a stern test, but the Spaniard raised his level in trademark fashion just when he needed it for a one-hour, 41-minute win.

Alcaraz had reeled off seven consecutive games from 1-1 in the first set to take complete control of Thursday’s encounter inside the Wiener Stadthalle, producing some typically showstopping all-court tennis. But he then let slip a break lead in the second set as last week’s Almaty finalist Basilashvili dug deep, and was forced to save four set points in the subsequent tie-break before converting his fourth match point for his 23rd consecutive win at ATP 500 level.

“I would say I played great, overall, from the beginning to the last point," Alcaraz said. "I played great tennis and I’m really happy with the performance that I did today. In the first set I was hitting the ball unbelievably and was feeling great on the court. I felt like he couldn’t play his style. Then in the second set I started pretty well, the same as the first set, but that game at 3-2, serving at him with a couple of mistakes, and he raised his level.

“I let him get into the match again. After that I would say it was really close. He was playing great, and obviously that tie-break. He had three easy balls to win the set, and I had three easy balls to win the match. I ended up missing the chances, but I’m just really happy with the way that I fought back.”

Next up for Alcaraz in Vienna is a last-eight meeting with Tommy Paul, who earlier raced past Luciano Darderi 6-1, 6-1. Alcaraz leads the seventh-seeded Paul 7-2 in the pair’s Lexus ATP Head2Head series and defeated the American in straight sets at both the Australian Open and US Open this year.

Paul is currently 12th in the PIF ATP Live Race To Turin, although his countryman Taylor Fritz could reclaim that position if he wins his second-round match in Basel on Thursday. Regardless, the 29-year-old Paul remains in outside contention to earn a debut qualification for the Nitto ATP Finals.

Daniil Medvedev also boosted his hopes of reaching the prestigious season finale, to be held in Turin from 15 to 22 November, with a second-round victory in Vienna. The former World No. 1 saved a match point on return when trailing Cameron Norrie 4-5, 40/30 in the third set before notching a 4-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) triumph.

Now into his 100th tour-level quarter-final (only the second man born since 1990 to achieve that feat after Alexander Zverev), Medvedev will meet qualifier Adrian Mannarino in the last eight. Medvedev is fifth in the Live Race, 551 points clear of Rafael Jodar in ninth, which is the qualification cutoff.

title: Why LIV Golf's latest crisis could have an unexpected Scottish upside
article_text:
Four years after LIV Golf turned the men’s professional game upside down, the question is no longer which stars it might lure away with Saudi riches, but whether the breakaway circuit can keep enough of them to survive.

After filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September, LIV is now trying to secure enough players and financial backing to launch a revamped version of the competition in 2027. That task has become harder as a stream of prominent players head for the exit. Jon Rahm, Adrian Meronk, David Puig, Louis Oosthuizen and Ian Poulter have all said their farewells.

For Scotland, this is more than distant turmoil: LIV players have become a significant presence at the Genesis Scottish Open and Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, raising the question of what their changing allegiances could mean for two of the country’s biggest tournaments.

Its proposed new financial backer, BC Partners, has lined up a potential funding package of up to $300 million aimed at keeping the league running. But the investor wants what has been described as a “critical mass” of players to commit to the new competition.

And that is the problem. Some of LIV’s most recognisable names have already decided against the new venture.

Rahm has provided the biggest blow, with his lawyer telling the bankruptcy court that the Spaniard regarded the terms offered for LIV 2.0 as unacceptable. Other departures have gathered pace, while Bryson DeChambeau, one of LIV’s most valuable remaining attractions, has yet to make a public commitment to LIV 2.0.

What has any of that got to do with Scotland?

Potentially quite a lot. Seven LIV players competed in July’s Genesis Scottish Open at the Renaissance Club in East Lothian, including Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Tom McKibbin, Meronk, Puig, Victor Perez and Laurie Canter. Their DP World Tour status provided a route into the event.

That route could now be closing for those who choose to remain with LIV. On October 12, the DP World Tour said players who sign up for LIV’s 2027 season will not be eligible for DP World Tour membership next year, forcing players to choose between the two circuits.

That matters in Scotland because the Scottish Open is jointly sanctioned by the DP World Tour and the US-based PGA Tour, LIV's principal established rival after the breakaway circuit launched in 2022. The complication is that several of those LIV players are now reconsidering where they will play their golf.

Probably an even better example. Meronk won this month’s Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, played across the Old Course at St Andrews, Carnoustie and Kingsbarns. The Pole finished 20 under par, two shots ahead of Casey Jarvis and Niklas Nørgaard, to win his fifth DP World Tour title and secure his tour status for 2027.

Within weeks he had decided he would not be part of LIV 2.0, with his Dunhill victory having secured his place on the DP World Tour for 2027.

His case illustrates why the consequences for Scotland are not necessarily negative. A golfer leaving LIV does not automatically disappear from Scottish fairways. If anything, playing a fuller DP World Tour schedule could potentially provide more opportunities to appear here.

Could LIV's problems actually be good news for Scottish tournaments?

Conceivably, although much depends on where the leading players go next.

There is already precedent for a golfer leaving LIV and concentrating on the DP World Tour. Patrick Reed declined a new LIV contract at the beginning of this year and has subsequently competed extensively on the European circuit, winning twice in 2026 as he seeks a route back to the PGA Tour.

That creates an intriguing possibility for the Scottish Open and Dunhill Links. If the upheaval at LIV sends more leading players towards the DP World Tour, Scottish events could find themselves with a bigger pool of familiar names to draw upon, rather than a smaller one.

There remains plenty of uncertainty. LIV is still trying to assemble a viable roster for 2027, while players must weigh up the financial attractions of its revamped model against opportunities elsewhere.

But Scotland has already developed an interesting position in golf’s long-running civil war. The Scottish Open brought LIV and PGA Tour players into the same field, while the Dunhill has offered another route into DP World Tour competition.

The irony, then, is that LIV spent four years pulling some of golf’s biggest names away from the established tours. Its present difficulties could now help send some of them back. Scotland could be one of the places where that change becomes most visible.

title: English-qualified winger commits future to Scotland amid Duhan van der Merwe uncertainty
article_text:
Edinburgh have secured the future of an exciting young winger amid uncertainty over Duhan van der Merwe’s long-term future at the club.

RUCK understands that Malelili Satala has signed a contract extension after attracting interest from several PREM Rugby clubs.

Leicester Tigers, Bristol Bears and Exeter Chiefs were all keen on the youngster, who has impressed since joining Edinburgh in 2025.

The 21-year-old is eligible to represent Scotland, England or Fiji at international level, having been born in Edinburgh.

His eligibility for Fiji comes through his father, Apolosi Satala, a former Edinburgh Rugby player who also served with the 1st Battalion Royal Regiment of Scotland.

Despite being born in Scotland, Satala grew up in Fiji before returning to the UK at the age of 16.

A dynamic back three player, the youngster has already showcased his pace and explosiveness.

Before returning to Scotland, Satala was part of Leicester Tigers’ senior academy. He made his senior debut in the Premiership Rugby Cup against Northampton Saints in November 2024, marking the occasion with a try.

Satala has since represented England U20s and Emerging Scotland, but is yet to earn a senior international cap.

His new deal comes at an important time for Edinburgh, with uncertainty surrounding the future of Scotland international Duhan van der Merwe.

Reports last week suggested the winger could leave the club when his contract expires next year, with a move to Japan or France among the possibilities.

According to Mail Sport, sources close to Edinburgh believe the 31-year-old is likely to move overseas, although no potential destinations have been identified.

Van der Merwe is approaching the latter stages of his career, and a move abroad could offer the winger an opportunity to take on a fresh challenge while securing a lucrative contract.

With what could be one of the final major deals of his career on the horizon, the Scotland international may look to maximise his earnings before hanging up his boots.

title: Defending Champion Miyu Yamashita Leads the LPGA's Maybank Championship After 2 Rounds
article_text:
KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia (AP) — Defending champion and world No. 4-ranked Miyu Yamashita shot a 6-under 66 Friday to take a two-stroke lead after two rounds of the LPGA Tour's Maybank Championship.

The 2025 Women's British Open winner had a two-round total of 13-under 131 on the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club course. She won last year's Malaysian tournament after a three-way playoff.

"I've been playing some really good rounds this year especially," Yamashita said. "My game is in better shape than last year, so my swing feels really good, too."

Julia Lopez Ramirez birdied three of her final four holes for a 66 and was tied for second with Pauline Roussin-Bouchard, who led by a stroke after the first round.

"Try to keep your mind cool and your body hydrated in these conditions," Lopez Ramirez said of her preparations for the weekend in the usual high humidity in Kuala Lumpur.

A Lim Kim had the round of the day, a 64, and was in fourth place, three strokes behind Yamashita.

Charley Hull had five birdies in her first six holes to move into the lead, but bogeyed two of her final three holes for a 69 and was tied for fifth, four strokes behind.

Haeran Ryu, a major winner this year at the Women's PGA Championship and at the Evian Championship, withdrew before her first-round tee time Thursday due to a strained finger ligament she suffered while riding in a golf cart during the Wednesday pro-am. She was the highest-ranked player in the tournament in the absence of No. 1 Nelly Korda and No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul.

Last week, Yuri Yoshida won the BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea, the fourth Japanese player this season to win on the LPGA Tour, joining Yamashita, Shiho Kuwaki and Yuna Nishimura. Yoshida shot 70 Friday and was at 5-under.

Next week, the LPGA's four-week, late-season Asian swing ends with the Toto Japan Classic at Omitama outside Tokyo.

title: Mexico Open: Karl Vilips shoots 62 to take the first-round lead with Marco Penge two shots back
article_text:
Karl Vilips used two long birdie streaks to take the first-round lead Thursday in the Mexico Open, the first of two straight PGA Tour events in the country.

Vilips shot a nine-under 62 in the afternoon round on the Vidanta Vallarta layout, making five straight birdies on Nos. 11-15 on his opening nine and finishing with four in a row. In between, he had another birdie and a bogey.

The 25-year-old Australian pointed to his driver.

"Had it on a string for the first nine," Vilips said. "Got a little loose in the middle and got it back on course toward the end of the round. It was lift, clean and place today so being in the fairway was a must for me and I took advantage of those drives that I hit."

Kensai Hirata of Japan was a stroke back, and Ben Griffin was at 64 with Marco Penge, Garrick Higgo and Jeffrey Kang.

Alvaro Ortiz of Mexico opened with a 65. He earned his PGA Tour card for next year through the Korn Ferry Tour.

"It was lovely," Ortiz said. "Bogey-free, played really solid. I felt like I was just flowing the whole day. Gave myself a lot of chances. I think I did very well from tee to green, which makes it very nice on this golf course."

Ortiz won the event in 2021 when it was part of the PGA Tour Latinoamerica schedule. The World Wide Technology Championship is next week at El Cardonal at Diamante in Los Cabos.

Vilips won the 2025 Puerto Rico Open for his lone PGA Tour title, making him exempt on the tour through next season.

The former Stanford player is 141st in the FedEx Cup Fall standings, with many players fighting to get into the final top 100 to remain on the tour.

Hirata is trying to move up from 170th. He made a 20-foot eagle putt on No. 3 and holed two birdie putts outside 20 feet.

"It was a perfect 7-wood distance and I hit a perfect 7-wood shot, which left me a really easy left-to-righter," Hirata said about the eagle. "Then that went in and kept the momentum going the rest of the back nine."

Penge is 112th in the standings. He had an 18-foot eagle putt on No. 3.

"I feel like I haven't actually played that much this year," Penge said "I've only played 18 tournaments due to, obviously, health issues. I'm just trying to get back fit really."

Defending champion Brian Campbell shot a 67.

Tom Kim also was at 67. He's playing for the first time since he won the gold medal in the Asian Games, which excuses him from mandatory military serve in South Korea.

U.S. Open champion Wyndham Clark had a 69. He's the only player from the top 10 in the world in the field.

John Daly II, the son of the two-time major champion, opened with a 70. He's playing on a sponsor exemption.

title: Can Nigeria’s Rugby Sevens Break Through in Africa?
article_text:
Nigerian sevens rugby has spent much of the past decade fighting simply to take the field, rebuilding its programme through suspensions, lost opportunities and long spells away from international competition. Now, with a settled coaching team and a growing pool of players at home and abroad, the question is whether the Stallions can turn steady progress into a genuine breakthrough.

Nigeria’s sevens story has often been shaped as much by decisions away from the pitch as by results on it. The side qualified for the 2014 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, only to be withdrawn, with Barbados taking its place.

A suspension that ended in 2017 was followed by another in 2021, after the Ministry of Sports dissolved the federation’s board, and that ban also cost the national 15s side its place in 2023 World Cup qualifying.

For a rugby nation stalled repeatedly by forces beyond its control, missing out on a regular calendar of rugby fixtures has been as damaging as any defeat.

Nigeria’s recent results show a team moving in the right direction without yet reaching the continent’s leading group.

The Stallions climbed from eleventh to seventh at the 2025 Africa Men’s Sevens, and at September’s SVNS 3 qualifier in Kampala they beat West African rivals Ghana but missed the semi-finals as Zimbabwe took Africa’s place.

The tournament showed both how close the chasing pack now is and how much ground Nigeria still has to make up.

Head coach Steve Lewis, who first led the Stallions in 2012, has built a squad that reflects the country’s reach well beyond its borders, with players based in Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and South Africa.

Three debutants, Onyekachi John-Osunkwo, Ayemere Alinafe Oiyemhonlan and Eze Kenechukwu, were selected to play in Kampala, adding depth to a group Lewis describes as combining experience with new talent. The federation’s stated objective is simple: build, compete, learn and progress.

The next opportunity is not far away, with World Rugby’s regional qualifiers for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics due in the second half of 2027.

Beyond that, the new sevens structure allows emerging nations to rise from regional qualification towards the elite level within a single season, rewarding teams that are ready when their chance arrives.

For Nigeria, breaking through will depend less on any one tournament than on whether players can compete season after season without the interruptions that have defined the programme’s past.
